title: Iterated Graph Systems (II): Bernoulli percolation and critical-exponent universality classes on hierarchical lattices
abstract: We study Bernoulli percolation and its universality classes on hierarchical lattices generated by edge iterated graph systems (EIGS). By examining eight critical exponents, we prove that no finite family of substitution-multiplicative dimensions completely determines universality, providing a rigorous proof of the failure of dimension-based universality discussed by Hauser and Saxena [Phys. Rev. B 34 (1986), 8193-8195]. Although the six exponentials theorem provides number-theoretic criteria for scale commensurability, we further disprove the conjecture that critical-exponent universality requires commensurate discrete renormalisation scales.
summary: This paper analyzes percolation on complex, self-similar hierarchical lattices defined by EIGS. It rigorously proves that the critical behavior (universality class) cannot be determined solely by geometric dimensions or by requiring commensurability of underlying scales. The work significantly advances the mathematical understanding of critical phenomena by showing the limitations of dimension-based classification.
main_problem: To rigorously investigate the universality classes of Bernoulli percolation on complex, self-similar hierarchical lattices generated by Edge Iterated Graph Systems (EIGS).
main_result: The study proves that universality cannot be determined by any finite set of substitution-multiplicative dimensions, and furthermore, it disproves the conjecture that critical-exponent universality requires commensurate renormalization scales.
method:
The authors use renormalization group techniques, analyzing various critical exponents ($ eta, 
u, \delta, \eta_{av}$) and relating them to geometric dimensions ($\dim_H, \dim_M, \dim_P$) derived from the EIGS structure.
model_or_system: The model is Bernoulli bond percolation on hierarchical lattices generated by deterministic or random Edge Iterated Graph Systems (EIGS). These lattices are characterized by specific rules graphs and associated geometric dimensions.
key_observables:
Critical exponents ($ eta, 
u, \delta, \eta_{av}$), ambient dimension ($\dim_H(\Xi)$), pivotal dimension ($\dim_P(C)$), and mass dimension ($\dim_M(C)$).
important_parameters: The percolation probability $p$ near the critical point $p_c$, and the structure of the underlying EIGS rule graph $R$.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the existence of specific geometric dimensions derived from the EIGS structure and the application of theorems related to number theory (e.g., six exponentials theorem).
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the structure of the Diamond Hierarchical Lattice (DHL) and compare the reliability functions and critical exponents for two different lattices ('Tie' and 'Gem') to demonstrate shared universality despite structural differences.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by defining the EIGS framework, establishing relationships between critical exponents and geometric dimensions, proving the failure of dimension-based universality, and finally constructing counterexamples to the requirement of commensurate renormalization scales.
why_interesting: While focused on classical percolation, the rigorous mathematical framework developed for classifying universality classes based on geometric invariants (dimensions) and the explicit disproof of simple dimensional criteria provides powerful, generalizable mathematical tools applicable to critical phenomena in quantum many-body systems.
